kiln_p19_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_001.text: The examination annex stood above a cart-repair shop, an unlikely place for ambition to become official. Yue climbed the narrow stairs carrying her habitual pack and no borrowed kiln apparatus. Luo followed with the agreed method record. The independent assessor met them in a plain room where the shutters admitted ordinary morning light and the bench had been cleared of someone else's ink pots. She asked Yue to put her name on the preparation sheet, not the qualification sheet. The distinction made her smile disappear for a moment. This visit would decide readiness and arrangements, without granting a rank.

kiln_p19_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_002.text: The assessor read the winter agreement before asking for any demonstration. Four distinct primary inward and outward pairs, the local reserve and compatible-charge thresholds, separate useful tasks, interruption and recovery. She asked who had supervised the new routes and which readings followed the shoulder injury. Luo supplied the dates and current physical limits. Yue added the stopped posterior attempt herself. The assessor looked up. 'I prefer a candidate who brings the page I would otherwise have to ask for.' Yue felt a brief warmth that had nothing to do with the apparatus and kept her hands still.

kiln_p19_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_003.text: The room's measuring equipment belonged to the examination service and had its own calibration history. The assessor and her assistant checked blanks, known loads, grounding capacity and contact positions before admitting Yue's personal input. Luo watched but did not set the independent readings. The useful task weights were small enough to look almost insulting beside the effort they had required. Yue remembered the first guarded quarter and swallowed the old urge to ask for something more impressive. A test could be demanding because it separated four routes accurately, not because it threatened to knock down the furniture.

kiln_p19_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_004.text: The dry route comparison went well until the assessor changed the naming order without warning. Yue identified both arms and the anterior leg pair, then hesitated at the posterior outward contact. She corrected it before input and described the distinct heel-calf-hip return. The assessor recorded the hesitation and asked whether it resembled earlier confusion. Yue showed the relevant pages. No charged task followed merely to erase the awkward moment. They repeated the dry mapping after rest, and the distinction stayed clear. Luo stood beside the door, letting the candidate and independent question meet without his familiar voice supplying the answer.

kiln_p19_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_005.text: The cart-repair worker had a daughter who wanted to watch the preparation visit. The assessor allowed her to see the cold apparatus demonstration from the public boundary, with no access to Yue's private bodily record. The girl asked why the task weight was smaller than her school bag. The assistant showed the independent interruption and the measured loss between input and useful work. She looked more interested after the explanation. Yue remembered her own disappointment at small weights. A task could become impressive through what it proved, provided nobody had to pretend the little receiver was secretly lifting a mountain.

kiln_p19_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_006.text: Another candidate arrived at the annex while Yue waited for the corrected blank. He trained under a different local method and asked whether thirty-six units were now required everywhere. The assessor said the threshold belonged to the agreed Azure Cloud four-pair examination. His own method needed its own qualified assessment and could not be converted through a casual comparison of numbers. The candidate looked relieved and annoyed at once. Yue liked him immediately for that familiar combination. They exchanged ordinary greetings, then returned to separate records. Neither person's useful result could become the other's rank by arithmetic alone.

kiln_p19_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_007.text: The other candidate asked if Yue had ever ridden a cart while gathering. She said her current supervised method and recovered posture were not a travel experiment. He admitted he had tried because the trip bored him and stopped when the receiving line drifted. The assessor invited the actual account into his preparation record and set the corresponding review. Yue kept out of his private findings. Their brief conversation still helped her feel less uniquely awkward. Other people also wanted progress to fill every empty hour and occasionally discovered that an empty hour had been serving a real purpose.

kiln_p19_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_008.text: The initial reserve reading appeared higher than Yue expected. She wanted the number to be true and disliked how quickly that desire arrived. The assessor asked for the sampling discharge and repeated the compatible fraction through the agreed comparison. A warm contact sleeve from the assistant's preceding equipment check affected the blank. The apparatus hadn't yet produced a valid candidate result. They cooled and rechecked it against the known blank before continuing. Yue sat through the delay with her hands open. A pleasing measurement could be wrong through ordinary conditions, and disappointment was a poor reason to rush its correction.

kiln_p19_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_009.text: The corrected post-sampling usable reserve was thirty-five and a quarter units, below the agreed thirty-six. Compatible charge measured just under ninety percent on the valid comparison. The assessor wrote both actual readings and declined to call the preparation visit a qualifying trial. Yue's four brief routes could still be reviewed within their recovered limits if useful for planning, but no successful weight would repair the failed admission threshold. She felt embarrassed in front of Luo, then saw his expression remain ordinary. He hadn't expected a date to produce a capacity. He had expected a person to report what she brought.

kiln_p19_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_010.text: 'I thought I was closer,' Yue said. The assessor answered that she was close in a way that required more recovered practice, not close in a way that changed the threshold. She gave no promise about how many days would be enough. The candidate could return when valid readings and ordinary recovery supported the formal sequence. Luo asked about the appointment window and the assessor offered a later reserved block with a preparation check beforehand. Yue agreed. An honest delay hadn't sent her back to the beginning. It had shown precisely which part of the next step was still missing.

kiln_p19_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_011.text: They left with the preparation result, equipment correction and revised dates. Yue wanted to go straight to a private practice circle and gather until the number looked better. Luo asked whether she had slept and eaten enough to make such a session recovered. She hadn't. They bought ordinary lunch at the cart-shop doorway instead. The repair worker gave them a stool with one short leg and called it an independently calibrated chair. Luo tested it and sat on the safer bench. Yue laughed for the first time since the reading. She bought another bun for the walk home.

kiln_p19_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_012.text: During lunch the annex assistant talked about her work, not Yue's chances. She wanted to become an independent examiner after completing the service's supervised course. Keeping known-load checks reliable had been less glamorous than she expected and more satisfying when she caught an error before a candidate relied on it. Yue asked whether the warm sleeve mistake would count against her. The assistant said the correction would remain in the equipment record and inform her training. She had no reason to hide it merely because the candidate was disappointed. Yue found that answer unexpectedly companionable.

kiln_p19_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_013.text: On the walk back, Luo asked what she feared the delay meant. Yue said she feared being a fourth-stage person who had spent months talking about fifth. He pointed out that she had spent months learning two actual new pairs, recovering a real injury and doing paid work. The final name did not make those months appear retrospectively. She knew the answer and still felt ashamed. He did not argue the feeling out of her. He told her when the next recovered session would occur, then asked whether she wanted the last half of his purchased bun. She did.

kiln_p19_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_014.text: Zhu welcomed them by demanding the examination gossip. Yue gave the readings and the delayed block. The trimmer held up two blue tiles that had looked identical before one failed the ordinary cleaning comparison. 'Welcome to the intolerable club of almost,' she said. Jian looked worried until Yue laughed. Peng entered the preparation result in the training packet without filing it as a formal failed qualifying trial; no qualifying trial had been admitted. No weight task had been assessed. Yue also kept it in her private notes, where a preparation disappointment could remain a day rather than an embarrassing absence.

kiln_p19_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_015.text: Luo bought a spare ink brush because the annex's borrowed one spread its strokes. Tan later teased him that no cultivation threshold had required an elegant signature. The foreman said a clear number wasn't elegance. Zhu borrowed the brush for a glaze label and returned it with a blue speck on the handle. Luo glared until she showed the fully cleaned bristles. Jian offered to make the speck a permanent maker's mark. The owner said the room already contained enough disputed authorship. Yue enjoyed the familiar noise after the independent room's quiet, where every question seemed to change her future.

kiln_p19_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_016.text: Peng inspected the training packet for legible source dates before transmission. She found a copied posterior repetition placed one day early in the index, while its actual session page and following check had the correct dates. Yue corrected the index and retained the correction, relieved that the error hadn't altered the bodily sequence. She had been tired while copying after the exhibition. Peng suggested finishing future indexes in a separate paid or personal hour, not in the exhausted margin of practice. Yue agreed. She chose a cooler copying hour before the next session.

kiln_p19_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_017.text: At the hall's ordinary assessments, Zhu watched a learner fail the rim comparison and succeed at the cold layout. He looked as though the mixed result meant he had failed as a whole person. She handed him both pages and said the next lesson would begin with the rim problem. Yue helped pack the models and thought of her preparation reading. A partial result was easiest to accept in someone else's record. She told Zhu this, and the trimmer answered, 'Then teach me while I assess you, and perhaps we'll both become tolerable.' Zhu handed her the models, still laughing.

kiln_p19_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_018.text: The following week began with a quieter gathering schedule under Luo's reviewed method. Yue admitted compatible input in the bounded source allowance, measured refinement loss and stopped before fatigue changed control. The usable reserve rose slowly after ordinary activity and sleep, not immediately upon opening a larger source. She did paid light work between sessions and kept the next-day movement checks. The posterior quarter-useful task remained at the recovered half input over four ordinary breaths. Nothing in the delayed examination permitted a larger pulse. Yue found steadiness boring for two days, then discovered that boredom itself could become restful.

kiln_p19_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_019.text: Her family reply arrived on the third day. The letter asked about wages, her shoulder and whether she enjoyed the town's food. It didn't demand a fifth-stage date. Her mother described an ordinary roof repair and a neighbor's spectacularly unsuccessful attempt to grow melons in a cold patch. Yue laughed aloud at the illustration in the margin. She had imagined home waiting with an examiner's stern face and found instead a household wanting her well. The relief did not change the usable reserve. It changed how tightly she held the morning's page, which was useful in an entirely different way.

kiln_p19_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_020.text: The owner invited Yue to remain for another teaching season if the later examination and work arrangements suited her. The offer concerned specified paid sample assistance and low-method preparation under qualified supervision, not an automatic senior post. Yue felt honored and trapped in the same instant. She had promised herself a road beyond the town, but the hall had become a place where people knew the true shape of her capacities. The owner let her take time to answer. She carried the unanswered offer upstairs and left it beside her notes.

kiln_p19_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_021.text: She asked Luo whether leaving after the assessment would seem ungrateful. He said gratitude had already appeared in her paid work, careful records and actual friendship. It did not require her to live forever beside his kiln. He would prefer a clear handover to an exhausted pupil staying out of guilt. Yue asked why good advice always sounded as though he had reached it through an inconvenient mistake. He looked toward the road where his daughter's household lay and said this one had taken several. The ordinary admission made her future feel less like a betrayal of their shared winter.

kiln_p19_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_022.text: Zhu said she would miss Yue and fully intended to make the departure inconvenient. She asked for letters containing useful road colors, ordinary gossip and honest failures, not only rank announcements. Yue promised letters when actual courier routes and money allowed them. The trimmer accepted the modest promise, then demanded a description of any kitchen that used sensible bowls. They argued about whether such a kitchen could exist. Jian listened from the next table and said he would like to visit one someday after finishing his actual course. He asked Peng when the next permitted visit would occur.

kiln_p19_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_023.text: Jian's mother sent a reply to the corrected household letter. The cousin's proposed position had gone to another qualified worker. She was disappointed about the lost opportunity and glad the claim was corrected before employment began. Jian read the letter twice. He had wanted honesty to make the offer wait for him. It hadn't. Yue sat with him without offering a better invented outcome. He asked whether the lost position meant the cold course was useless. She pointed to his safely completed task and asked him to answer the question from that actual page instead of the cousin's calendar.

kiln_p19_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_024.text: He said the page meant he could report a changed condition before making it somebody else's problem. That capacity would be useful anywhere, though not a promise of immediate employment. Yue nodded. The boy folded the letter and returned to the copying task. Later he asked Tan about ordinary vacancies that matched his present allowed skills. The clerk named actual possibilities and their wages, without arranging a hidden favor. Jian chose to remain through the review period because the funded course was real. He could still seek future work afterward. He wrote the present choice in his household reply.

kiln_p19_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_025.text: Han saw the vacancy list and asked whether the boy was leaving. Jian explained the actual choice. Han said the kitchen could use a reliable cold sample runner for the next permitted visit, with the supervisor present. It was an ordinary work suggestion within the restriction, not a request to share the hot post. Jian accepted too quickly, then checked the roster before promising a time. Han noticed and smiled faintly. Yue kept sorting labels. She didn't want either man to feel watched like a display object whenever he made a useful civil gesture. Their work could belong to them.

kiln_p19_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_026.text: Peng asked whether the kitchen final prototype feedback had arrived. Yue brought the revised capacity and grip notes, plus the caretaker's acceptance of the limited ordinary trial. Zhu still needed to finalize the body and production schedule after the current summer deliveries. The full commission remained proposed, not promised. Tan arranged a later commercial meeting that did not conflict with the examination block. Yue saw the hall resist making her rank a condition of every future order. The kitchen needed sound ordinary bowls. It could receive them whether her assessment took a week, a month or another patient season.

kiln_p19_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_027.text: The kitchen's washer came with a humorous drawing of the old overlarge bowl beside a starving purse. Zhu pinned the permitted copy near the ordinary prototype series. It made the capacity correction memorable without turning the customer's budget into a joke against him. The washer liked seeing his own practical criticism retained. He asked if future makers would know who suggested the grip change. Peng showed him the attributed note. Yue saw a form of apprenticeship credit beyond any formal apprentice: a user had contributed knowledge and would not disappear behind the maker's lovely final glaze.

kiln_p19_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_028.text: Tan wanted the proposed kitchen order to carry a grand title for the exhibition commendation. The caretaker wanted a delivery list she could understand. He drafted both and watched Zhu cross out the title that claimed exceptional cultivation. No charge entered the ordinary bowls. The useful design came from material trials, user feedback and paid craft. Tan sighed theatrically and wrote the plain title. Yue said the resulting order sounded less expensive already. He replied that he would preserve at least one beautiful comma. The caretaker accepted the revised proposal and kept the production decision pending the available schedule.

kiln_p19_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_029.text: Jian reached the end of his sixth remedial week and asked the representative what the eight-week check would examine. He wanted to prepare without guessing at a hidden demand for remorse. The independent reviewer would consider truthful reporting, completed safe cold tasks, response to changed conditions and the safety arrangement. Live reinstatement wouldn't follow from good manners alone. Han's actual roster concerns would be heard. The boy wrote the answers down and admitted he wished the check could guarantee qualification. Yue understood the wish. A known date was easier to picture than a capacity another person would examine without affection.

kiln_p19_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_030.text: Han's latest care review found continued healing and allowed a carefully limited return to one inspected warm task closer to the main hall. The original grit post remained outside the schedule until the final relevant check. He wanted to take the new task because he missed the ordinary crew, not because anybody required a public display of confidence. The owner assigned another qualified worker alongside him and retained the care conditions. Jian stayed in the cold room during the task. Yue watched Han finish and ask for regular tea. His useful return didn't need the boy present to become meaningful.

kiln_p19_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_031.text: At the evening table Han asked Yue about the preparation reading. She described the warm sleeve and valid correction. He said the repair bench had once fooled him with a lovely straight edge that was itself bent. 'Never trust an attractive reference without knowing who checked it,' he said. Zhu asked if the advice included people. He replied that people were usually less straight than rulers. Jian laughed and then offered the kitchen model's crooked first foot as evidence. The table shook with laughter. Yue went upstairs grateful that serious work could still produce absurd ordinary conversations.

kiln_p19_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_032.text: The next compatible-fraction check reached ninety percent on the valid comparison, with usable reserve still just below thirty-six after sampling. Luo held the page as progress, not admission. Yue tried to be disappointed about only one missing threshold instead of two. He said the thresholds weren't a race against each other. Their simultaneous recovered presence mattered. She repeated the known routes on the permitted days and rested through a hot afternoon when sleep had been poor. The source allowance remained finite and recorded. She slept through the next quiet night and checked the result again.

kiln_p19_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_033.text: A hot spell forced another change in Yue's rest. The lodging room stayed warm after sunset, and she slept poorly despite lying quietly. Luo didn't classify lying down as recovered sleep. She moved the next practice task and spent the cooler morning beneath the archive stairs preparing ordinary copies. Peng found a fan and passed it over without ceremony. Yue joked that it was the most effective cultivation artifact in the building. Peng said it was an ordinary fan with a bent rib and required an ordinary user's wrist. Peng fanned the page dry before turning it.

kiln_p19_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_034.text: The owner arranged a cooler room for the examination nights, part of the agreed local accommodation provision rather than an unexplained luxury. Yue checked that using it did not displace an injured worker. Han had his separate care space and ordinary lodging choice. The room's window faced a shaded wall, and its mattress smelled faintly of clean straw. She slept well there after an ordinary day and reported the actual result. A recovery arrangement could improve the conditions without doing the bodily work for her. She would still have to arrive with normal touch, grip and leg movement.

kiln_p19_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_035.text: Zhu invited her to watch the first paid cold teaching session built from the revised prerequisite model. The learner centered the body before comparing the rim, and the larger model let everyone see the supported foot. The session still ran long. Zhu asked for feedback instead of declaring the extra time proof of enthusiasm. Two learners wanted more individual practice, which required actual future hours. The owner approved a second group rather than crowd the bench. Yue watched the negotiation with new interest. Zhu set the larger model beside the next learner and began again.

kiln_p19_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_036.text: After the lesson, Yue asked whether Zhu might want to study a low cultivation method someday. The trimmer said perhaps, if her hand's condition and a qualified teacher allowed it, but not as a requirement for her ordinary craft to matter. Yue heard the answer as a correction to her own easy assumption. Zhu already wanted paid instruction, deep blue glaze and a useful bowl shape. A cultivation rank could become another choice later. It didn't have to be the hidden final chapter of every talented worker's life. Yue apologized for making the question sound like an offer of completion.

kiln_p19_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_037.text: Zhu accepted the apology and said she would complete her life by finding lunch. They bought ordinary noodles from a stall whose bowls were visibly mismatched. The seller called this artistic diversity. Zhu lifted one with a chipped foot and told him it was a poorly qualified example of the genre. He gave her a discount for the joke and replaced the unstable bowl before serving. Yue enjoyed the meal without turning every table into a craft review. Then a loud argument began over someone else's borrowed chopsticks, and the town restored their humility with the regular price of inconvenience.

kiln_p19_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_038.text: The communal kitchen sent its caretaker and washer to the hall for the revised prototype inspection. They liked the smaller capacity and clean external mark. Zhu showed the retained failed body and the successful current comparison, keeping the use limits clear. The washer tried the cold grip and stacking arrangement himself. He asked for one further ordinary foot adjustment, which could be reviewed before production. Tan marked the proposal as pending that check. Yue noticed the customer becoming an author of the useful object. The eventual fair commission would include his awkward practical needs, not just a maker's pleasing drawing.

kiln_p19_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_039.text: Luo approved the small foot adjustment for a new ordinary comparison within the sample plan. It passed the defined use tests after actual drying and firing, with the retained piece inspected rather than declared equivalent by appearance. The commercial meeting could now offer a qualified shape and an achievable staged schedule. The owner postponed signing until the current promised orders were delivered and the resources were free. Nobody used the delay to threaten the kitchen with losing its place unless it paid an advance immediately. Yue admired the restraint more than the earlier dramatic refusal of the impossible winter contract.

kiln_p19_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_040.text: Before the formal block, Su Yan reviewed the full route and recovery packet on another planned circuit stop. She examined Yue's ordinary movement, asked about the shoulder and watched a dry changed-order map. The new posterior pair remained distinct from the anterior pair; both retained their own inward and outward returns. She didn't add extraordinary vessels or teach a continuous circuit because four routes now worked briefly. Yue asked if she should know more before the examination. Su Yan said knowledge of limits counted among the useful things she already needed to know. Then she asked whether Yue had eaten.

kiln_p19_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_041.text: At supper the teacher spoke with Luo about actual replenishment between trials. The finite source block had been reserved and qualified, with enough allowance for recorded gathering, refinement loss and sampling. It was not the commercial firing supply. Nobody would lend personal reserve to make the candidate's readings pass. Yue would have ordinary activity, sleep and recovered checks before each trial rather than live in an artificially motionless bubble. Su Yan approved the schedule and declined an invitation to stay as an examiner. Independence meant the final assessment would not be her own affection signing its conclusion.

kiln_p19_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_042.text: Yue asked why teacher affection always appeared in warnings as if it were a contaminant. Su Yan smiled. 'Because it is a good thing with a particular weakness.' It helped a teacher remain through slow failures; it could tempt the same teacher to see a wished-for success too soon. The independent assessor didn't need to care less about the candidate's safety. She needed to arrive without their shared story deciding the result. Yue liked the explanation more than a stern claim that examinations possessed pure objectivity. People checked other people, and the arrangement had to admit what each person brought.

kiln_p19_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_043.text: The next ordinary movement review found Yue's shoulder comfortable through the current partnered waist work, with no new deficit. Sudden overhead catching still hadn't been reassessed and remained outside clearance. The leg movements and sensation were normal after the recovered new-pair tasks. The clinician signed the physical findings, not the cultivation rank. Yue carried that page to the packet and noticed how several qualified roles now supported the assessment without one pretending to replace the others. A doctor could clear movement, a teacher could describe practice, an examiner could assess the method. The candidate still had to do the work.

kiln_p19_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_044.text: Her next valid reserve reading reached thirty-six and a half units after sampling discharge, with ninety percent compatible charge. She had slept normally after an ordinary paid day, and the movement checks were clean. Luo didn't promote her. He transmitted the actual readiness page to the independent assessor and planned another recovered confirmation before the formal window. Yue sat staring at the half unit above the threshold. It looked absurdly small beside the months, yet its presence was not invented. She asked whether she could celebrate. Luo said certainly, provided celebration did not become a sleepless evening that invalidated tomorrow.

kiln_p19_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_045.text: She bought fruit for the supper table with her own wages and left the borrowed measuring tools where they belonged. Zhu demanded an exact explanation for the feast, and Yue gave the readiness result without calling it a completed rank. Jian proposed a toast to a half unit that had taken longer to arrive than a cart from the capital. Peng said carts didn't usually undergo purity sampling. Han raised his cup and wished her ordinary sleep. Yue drank her water and thanked him. She went upstairs before the fruit story could grow into an all-night event.

kiln_p19_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_046.text: The following day's ordinary touch, grip and leg movement were normal. A later recovered confirmation found more than thirty-six usable units after sampling and just over ninety percent compatible charge on the valid apparatus. Luo sent that result too. The assessor confirmed the examination block, still conditional on each day's actual readiness and recovery. Yue wouldn't be allowed to bank a good reading now and ignore a poor one during a formal trial. She put the letter beside the two readiness pages. Then she put the apparatus note away and opened Zhu's latest color sketch.

kiln_p19_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_047.text: On the annex's market street, Yue found a stall selling painted examination charms. One promised perfect recall through a paper tiger of doubtful anatomy. It reminded her of Luo's grandchild's carving. She bought no charm, but paid for a small ordinary postcard of the town kiln road to send home. The seller asked if she would like a lucky border. Yue chose the cheaper plain one and said her family would recognize the road without it. The decision felt pleasantly unimportant. Not every choice on the way to advancement needed to become a principle worth teaching.

kiln_p19_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_048.text: She wrote the postcard after the next readiness check, describing the town's mismatched noodle bowls and Zhu's gray tile. The fifth stage appeared only as a hoped-for assessment still ahead. Her letter had already carried the technical progress. The small card could carry weather, jokes and a picture her younger relatives would enjoy. Peng helped identify the actual postal route without reading the message. Yue paid the price and went back to the comparison room. She felt less lonely because home could receive ordinary life from her, not only evidence that the journey had justified its cost.

kiln_p19_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_049.text: At the annex's second preparation visit, Yue checked the borrowed room's ordinary conditions with the assistant. The shutter draft had changed after a window repair, and the bench had been moved to avoid direct afternoon heat. The apparatus could be calibrated there, but the old floor marks were no longer enough. They laid the permitted contact positions from the actual receiver and grounded boundary. Yue enjoyed seeing the independent service revise its own setup. The examiner was not perfect because she held authority. She was useful because she checked a changed room before asking the candidate to perform in it.

kiln_p19_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_050.text: The independent assessor offered the candidates a cold orientation to the formal stop probes. Each probe used a small bounded fraction distinct from the useful task, with enough ground capacity and no useful-load claim. Yue practiced the ordinary control motion without charge until she could interrupt without reaching across the receiver. The assessor would vary the permitted signal within the stated task, not invent an unsafe surprise. The preparation made Yue less anxious about what independence meant. An examiner could test unprompted control honestly while still telling the candidate the physical boundary in which the question would occur.

kiln_p19_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_051.text: The trial order would change among the four distinct pairs, preventing one comfortable sequence from carrying the whole assessment. Rest and complete grounded discharge separated every pair. Yue asked whether the changed order might mean doing two leg tasks continuously to save time. The assessor said no. Independence was precisely what the rest and separation helped reveal. The exam wouldn't imply a continuous six-pair circuit from a few brief tasks. Yue repeated the dry maps in the permitted order and left the apparatus untouched afterward. She left the apparatus grounded and went downstairs for lunch.

kiln_p19_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_052.text: The assessor explained the formal sequence in advance. Three qualifying trials on separate recovered days would change the permitted order of the four pairs. Each pair would do its quarter useful task at the bounded input, demonstrate independent interruption on a separate probe, discharge fully and rest. The reserve and compatible fraction would be checked after sampling before each trial. The probes' costs and useful-task input would come from Yue's actual reserve, never the teacher's charge. Each following day required ordinary touch, grip and leg-movement checks. A failed condition would stop the sequence regardless of a final weight.

kiln_p19_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_053.text: The actual task total and interruption-probe cost would leave less reserve afterward than before. This was expected expenditure, not a reason to measure only the flattering earlier number. Yue would rest, eat and replenish within the permitted finite source allowance between trial days, then meet the thresholds anew after ordinary activity and sleep. The assessor would record both readings and the replenishment rather than call the reserve inexhaustible. Luo agreed the schedule allowed enough recovered time. Yue asked one practical question about the probe receiver, and the assistant answered with a cold demonstration before any input was admitted.

kiln_p19_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_054.text: The room fee covered the actual reserved hours and assistant's work. Tan confirmed it from the agreed teaching and examination provision before the formal block began. Yue would not owe an unknown successful-candidate surcharge afterward. If recovery forced a rescheduled day, the stated additional room cost would be decided before booking. The financial clarity left her free to fear the actual test instead of a hidden bill. She joked about this with Zhu, who said the hall was improving at producing honest anxieties. They bought two cheap summer fruits and split them beneath the shaded wall.

kiln_p19_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_055.text: Before leaving, the assessor asked what the candidate intended to do with a fifth-stage record. Yue said she wanted to continue learning and perhaps teach the low method honestly someday. She also wanted the pleasure of knowing she had earned it. The assessor smiled at the second answer. Ambition didn't have to disguise itself entirely as service. The record would qualify only the brief routes and local thresholds, not unknown tools, untested bodily reinforcement or higher circuits. Yue repeated that boundary and asked for it on the final record if she passed. She touched the empty record cover and smiled.

kiln_p19_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_056.text: Luo and Yue descended the cart-shop stairs together. The broken-legged stool had been repaired; the worker proudly invited them to perform another independent assessment. Luo sat on it this time and declared the result tolerable. Yue bought two buns and chose the bench where the shadow was coolest. The preparation month had given her enough confidence to laugh without pretending the final trials were easy. She ate slowly and listened to the hammer below. Tomorrow would still require rest. The day after that might begin the first qualifying trial, if the person reached morning in the condition the method required.

kiln_p19_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_057.text: Back at the hall, Jian's eight-week check was scheduled for the same fortnight as her formal trials. Neither assessment would become the other's proof. The boy said he wished every important thing did not arrive together. Peng showed him the ordinary calendar: kiln deliveries, teacher leave, kitchen meeting, clinic follow-up and two examinations. The world had been busy all along. Yue helped him prepare the permitted task packet without writing his account for him. He helped check the dates in her training index. They could support each other's work while leaving the actual decision to independent eyes.

kiln_p19_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_058.text: Jian helped check the packet's page order under Peng's copying supervision. He had no authority to alter readings or supply an observation he had not witnessed. He caught a duplicated index leaf and removed the duplicate while retaining the actual route pages. Yue thanked him for the ordinary competence. He said it was less exciting than bringing an inspector by changing a vent. Then his smile disappeared. 'That was a terrible joke.' She said yes, and let him apologize without either magnifying or excusing it. Their friendship could survive an awkward sentence if they kept noticing what the sentence did.

kiln_p19_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_059.text: At the next remedial session he told the teacher about the joke and why he regretted it. The account was not treated as a new mechanical violation or proof of inevitable future sabotage. It was part of learning how his words affected people after a real harm. The teacher asked him to think about the audience before using that particular memory for humor. Jian wrote the note and went on with the actual cold task. Yue was glad the course could respond proportionately. Every embarrassment did not need a new punishment, just as every apology did not restore live access.

kiln_p19_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_060.text: Han asked Yue whether she would show him the fifth-stage record if she earned it. She said yes, with the useful limits attached. He wanted to know which things a customer might wrongly demand from her afterward. They made a ridiculous list: lifting the town well, purifying soup, carrying a cart on one toe. Zhu added making an unstable bowl stand through sheer moral conviction. Yue laughed and then wrote the actual boundary in her private summary: brief calibrated receiving tasks, no automatic self-reinforcement, unknown apparatus qualification or continuous circuit. The jokes had given the limit an ordinary voice.

kiln_p19_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_061.text: The evening before the first planned formal day, Luo said nothing inspirational. He checked that Yue knew the morning time, had the actual readiness pages and intended to sleep. Then he went downstairs to review an ordinary kiln schedule. Zhu brought a clean cloth for the shaded room and refused to stay talking. Jian wished her a boring successful morning. Han sent word that breakfast would be breakfast, not a banquet with an omen hidden in every bowl. Yue lay down smiling. The people who wanted her to pass had finally given her something simpler than encouragement: room to recover.

kiln_p19_062.speaker: narrator
kiln_p19_062.text: At the close of the thirty-third week, Yue slept in the room she had known through winter pain and spring uncertainty. Her habitual pack waited beside the bed, containing wages, personal notes and a record still naming the fourth stage. The next rank hadn't entered through a dream, a number or a flattering letter. Two additional distinct pairs had learned brief work over months; reserve and compatible fraction now met the agreed readiness readings. The independent trials remained ahead. She extinguished the lamp and listened to the hall settle, then fell asleep before her ambition could begin another imaginary examination.
